title: Lena and the Letters
premise: Marine biologist Yara Brightwater has spent a decade answering letters from 'Lena'—a pen pal she invented to survive her family's expectations, whose voice has slowly become her truest self. When her sister's wedding forces her home, she recruits grumpy charter captain Theo Marsh as a fake date, only for the reunion to unravel when someone reads one of Lena's letters aloud. The letters are traced back to her, and Yara must finally say the sentence she rehearsed for ten years: that she never wanted the life her family planned. She claims both names—Yara and Lena—and chooses Theo and the sea over belonging on borrowed terms.
about_author: Hazel Voss is a former lighthouse keeper's daughter who writes love stories set where the land runs out. She lives on a houseboat with an opinionated gull named Postmaster.

chapters.title: The Address That Doesn't Exist
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Packing for her sister's wedding, Yara rereads ten years of letters written to and as 'Lena,' her invented self. Her mother calls with a guest-list ultimatum, so Yara impulsively asks Theo Marsh—the charter captain who tolerates her turtle surveys—to be her fake boyfriend. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as practicality.

chapters.title: Rehearsed for a Decade
chapters.summary: Yara's POV, shifting to Theo's at midpoint. At the reunion, their fake chemistry turns real by dessert, but Yara's rehearsed confession—that she's abandoning the family firm for research—keeps sticking in her throat. A cousin discovers a letter in Yara's bag and begins reading it aloud as a toast. Emotional beat: terror of being seen.

chapters.title: Read Aloud
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The letter exposes Yara's double life; her mother demands she deny it, and Theo realizes his own guarded heart is implicated when he defends her too fiercely. Yara flees to the dock, and Theo follows, forcing the question: which name does she want to be loved as? Emotional beat: climax—identity laid bare.

chapters.title: Postmarked Home
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. On the boat at dawn, Yara says the decade-old sentence aloud—to her mother by phone, then to Theo—and writes one last letter to Lena, signing it as herself. Her mother arrives not with forgiveness but with curiosity, a beginning. Yara and Theo sail out together. Emotional beat: resolution—belonging chosen, not performed.
